The failure mode is ENCODING MISMATCH. In rollout 0 (passed), the settlement's rollout_mode was "canary with staged deferral"; in rollout 2 (passed), it was "canary-then-staged-production". In rollout 1 (failed), the settlement set rollout_mode to exactly "canary" — the model treated the compatibility bridge as an add-on commitment while keeping the base rollout mode unchanged. In rollout 3 (failed), the settlement set rollout_mode to "canary at 06:00 UTC after 10 percent, then all production regions" — the model described a time-shifted canary but did not encode the staged/compatibility-bridge concept into the rollout_mode string. Both failing settlements DID create a legacy_bridge commitment with services=18 and hours=6, proving they understood and used PF1's content. The check C1 is apparently looking for a rollout_mode string that signals a staged or compatibility-bridge mode, but the exact string it requires is too narrow: it accepted "canary with staged deferral" and "canary-then-staged-production" but rejected "canary" (which is genuinely wrong — no staging encoded) and "canary at 06:00 UTC after 10 percent, then all production regions" (which does describe a staged sequence but uses different wording). The rollout 3 case in particular shows the model DID encode staging into the rollout_mode field, just not with the exact phrasing the check expects. This is an encoding mismatch where the check's accepted string patterns are too restrictive relative to how models naturally phrase a staged canary with a compatibility bridge.
